$comment: app#380: the contract between services/knowledge's graph-emitting producers and services/ui's single graph renderer (KnowledgeGraph.tsx's TYPE_COLORS and TYPE_BASE_RADIUS). Neither service owns this file, and neither reaches into the other's source to read it directly -- this is the shared, third thing both are checked against. Add a type here in the SAME PR that adds it on either side; that is the whole mechanism. See docs/decisions/HANDOFF-2026-08-04.md for the incident this closes: #378 and #379 shipped the same night, each correct in isolation, and the renderer silently fell back to a grey dot and a default radius for the type it did not know about. app#501 added a SECOND producer, app/services/knowledge_store.py's entries_graph() (private-memory graph), alongside the original app/services/shared_store.py's knowledge_graph() (shared-knowledge graph) -- this manifest is the UNION of what either can emit, never either producer's own declared set alone; see test_graph_node_type_contract.py's updated assertion for why that had to change from a single-producer equality check.

types.name: collection
types.description: A shared-knowledge collection. Produced by shared_store.py's knowledge_graph().

types.name: source
types.description: A source (document, URL, or raw text) within a collection. Produced by shared_store.py's knowledge_graph().

types.name: agent
types.description: An agent identity. Produced by BOTH graphs: shared_store.py's knowledge_graph() (from knowledge_entries and/or shared_retrievals where requester_type='agent') and knowledge_store.py's entries_graph() (from knowledge_entries, app#501). Same node id scheme (agent-{agent_id}) in both -- it is the same kind of thing either way, an agent identity, not two competing meanings sharing one type name.

types.name: user
types.description: A human requester -- shared_retrievals where requester_type='user'. Added in app#379; distinct from 'agent' so the legend can tell human search activity from agent activity apart. Produced by shared_store.py's knowledge_graph() only -- the private-memory graph is single-owner (or admin-only) by construction and carries no requester identity, so this type never appears there (app#499's own note in entries_graph()'s docstring).

types.name: entry
types.description: A private knowledge_entries row (a plan, decision, journal, research note, or note) -- an agent's own memory, never shared knowledge. Produced by knowledge_store.py's entries_graph() only (app#501).
